title: SLO lease & borrowing policy for regional capacity with cost-aware load-shedding
creator: Samantha Liu
description:
Summary:
This ticket defines and implements a policy for SLO leasing and error-budget borrowing across regions, combined with a cost-aware load-shedding strategy and model-level circuit-breakers. The goal is to keep high-priority customers and latency-sensitive routes within SLOs during region-level capacity pressure while minimizing overall cost and preserving degraded-but-useful functionality for lower-priority traffic.

Problem context:
- We operate multi-region inference clusters with variable capacity and cost profiles (e.g., us-west cheaper spot pools, eu-central higher reserved).
- During regional overloads or outages we currently either: failover entirely (higher cost/latency), or degrade all traffic equally, which is suboptimal for prioritized customers and expensive for cost-sensitive workloads.
- There is no formal mechanism to temporarily "borrow" error budget or lease capacity across regions with bounded time and cost governance.

Design goals:
1) SLO leasing: enable a region to borrow a bounded amount of error budget from another region or a global pool for specific endpoints/models for a limited lease time. Leases are recorded, enforceable, and automatically reclaimed.
2) Cost-aware routing: incorporate regional cost multiplier and model cost (GPU seconds) into routing decisions so failover favors cheaper alternatives where latency allows.
3) Progressive circuit-breakers: per-model and per-route circuit-breaker states (healthy, degraded, shed) with thresholds tied to composite SLI (latency, success rate, quality).
4) Load-shedding hierarchy: when shedding is necessary, prefer shedding by model-cost and quality-risk ordering (longer-gen models, expensive quantized variants first), preserving short/cheap completions and critical customers.
5) Observability and runbooks: clear dashboards, error-budget ledgers, and playbook for manual overrides and audit.

Scope:
- Define SLI/SLO schema for per-endpoint/per-model SLO leases, including metrics and labels.
- Implement error-budget ledger and lease API in router/policy engine.
- Extend traffic router to use cost multipliers and lease state for routing decisions.
- Implement circuit-breaker state machine and load-shedding actions in router.
- Dashboards and alerting for lease exhaustion, cross-region borrow rate, and shed events.
acceptance_criteria: Formal SLI definitions for latency (p50/p95/p99), success_rate (200/5xx), and model_quality (evaluation-based proxy) for per-endpoint and per-model SLOs are published in the team Confluence.
Error-budget ledger exists per region per model with APIs to create/consume/lease/return budgets; lease records include tenant, duration, and cost multiplier.
Router consults lease + cost multipliers + circuit-breaker state and produces deterministic routing decisions (unit tests + integration tests).
Progressive circuit-breaker triggers and load-shedding actions implemented: soft-throttle -> partial-shed (low-cost models preserved) -> hard-shed for non-critical traffic.
Dashboards show live error-budget usage, outstanding leases, cross-region borrow metrics, and shed events; alerts created for >80% global borrow and any hard-shed occurrence.
Canary rollout performed against staging traffic with fault-injection scenarios (simulated region capacity loss) and postmortem demonstrating restored SLOs for critical routes.
Runbook documenting manual lease revocation, emergency cost cap, and rollback steps is committed and linked from the console.
implementation_notes:
Technical outline:
1) Metric definitions: add dimension 'slo_scope' = {endpoint, model, customer_tier}. SLIs exported: request_latency_ms_p50/p95/p99, request_success_fraction (>=200 and <500), model_quality_estimate (from offline eval harness sampled 1:1000).
2) Error-budget ledger: new service 'slo-ledger' exposing GRPC endpoints ledger.CreateLease(tenant, region_from, region_to, amount_tokens, ttl_seconds, cost_multiplier) and ledger.Consume(lease_id, amount). Leases auto-expire.
3) Router changes: policy-engine consults ledger.balance(region, model) and active_leases; uses score = latency_penalty * SLA_weight + cost_multiplier * cost_weight + quality_penalty; pick route with lowest score respecting lease constraints.
4) Circuit-breakers: implement per-variant sliding-window error counters and dynamic thresholds that decay with recovered throughput. Include mode 'probe' to test reopened variants at low QPS.
5) Load-shedding: define shed tiers: T0 (critical customers / internal), T1 (paid tier), T2 (free). Within a tier, order models by expected GPU-ms per request and model_quality_risk. Shedding action labels: 'soft-throttle', 'route-variant-to-cheaper', 'partial-drop', 'hard-drop'.
6) Telemetry: emit events slo.lease.created/expired/consumed, slo.shed.event, slo.circuit_breaker.{open,half_open,closed}. Tag events with request id, tenant, model, region, cause.
rollout_plan:
1) Spec review (this ticket) -> 1 week. 2) Implement slo-ledger and router read path in feature branch. 3) Unit + integration tests in staging. 4) Canary (5% traffic) for non-critical routes with injected region failures. 5) Monitor for 48h, escalate if hard-shed events > 5/hour or cost increases exceed budget cap. 6) Ramp to 25% -> 50% -> 100% over two weeks.
Manual gates: PM sign-off after staging tests; SRE on-call present during first 3 days of canary.
monitoring_and_alerting:
Dashboards: 'SLO Ledger Overview', 'Cross-Region Borrowing Heatmap', 'Load-shedding Timeline', 'Circuit-breaker States by Model'.
Alerts: P0 if global borrow > 80% for > 10m; P1 if any critical customer experiences > 5% hard-shed in 5m window; P1 if canary causes latency p95 regression > 20% for critical routes.
tests_and_validation: Unit tests for ledger lease semantics and auto-expiration.
Integration tests: router routing decision matrix with mocked cost multipliers and lease states.
Chaos test in staging: simulate region CPU/GPU saturation and validate expected shed hierarchy and leased fallback behavior.
Cost simulation to ensure leasing doesn't exceed monthly cost cap (automated nightly job).
User acceptance test with Solutions Eng: simulate enterprise customer traffic and verify preservation of critical endpoints under load.
